subject: common kestrel
title: Voles Hide in the Grass. Kestrels Follow Their Glowing Pee

scenes.text: Voles hide perfectly in long grass. Their own pee gives them away.
A vole marks its runways with squirts of urine, all day long.
To us, those trails are invisible. Not to a kestrel hovering above.
Kestrels see ultraviolet light, and vole urine shows up in ultraviolet.
In Finland, scientists laid fake urine trails where no voles lived. Kestrels came and searched them anyway.
So the vole's map of home is also the hunter's map to dinner.

description:
Voles mark their runways with urine, and that urine reflects ultraviolet light, which kestrels can see.
In a 1995 study in Finland, kestrels were drawn to artificial vole urine trails laid where no voles lived.
What other hunter would you want us to cover?
first_comment: Kestrels can hover in one spot with their head almost perfectly still. Which other animal sees colours we can't?
